column1: # How people actually type Gujarati in Latin letters, and what they mean by it.
# Two kinds of spelling are here, and neither is reachable from the phonetic
#  - Words the rules get wrong because Latin spelling does not carry the
#    difference: a long vowel nobody doubles ("maru" is મારું, "pani" is
#    પાણી), dental against retroflex ("mate" is માટે, "thodu" is થોડું), ણ and
#    ળ typed as plain n and l ("pan" is પણ, "dal" is દાળ), ષ typed as sh
#    ("bhasha" is ભાષા), gemination nobody types ("papa" is પપ્પા).
#  - Chat shorthand: "che" / "chu" / "cho" for છે / છું / છો, "su" for શું,
# What the rules already do is left out: final -u is the neuter -ું (hu હું,
# karvu કરવું), locative -ma is માં, -vanu is વાનું.
# A hand-written draft of the commonest few hundred words that wants a Gujarati
# Format: spelling<TAB>gujarati   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
